paragraphs: Hillman Solutions Corp. and its wholly-owned subsidiaries (collectively, "Hillman" or "Company") are one of the largest providers of hardware-related products and related merchandising services to retail markets in North America. Our principal business is operated through our wholly-owned subsidiary, Hillman, which had net sales of approximately $1,552.2 million in 2025. Hillman sells its products to hardware stores, home centers, mass merchants, pet supply stores, and other retail outlets principally in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Latin America, and the Caribbean. Product lines include thousands of small parts such as fasteners and related hardware items; threaded rod and metal shapes; keys; builder's hardware; personal protective equipment, such as gloves and eye-wear; rope and chain; and identification items, such as tags and letters, numbers, and signs. We support product sales with services that include design and installation of merchandising systems, maintenance of appropriate in-store inventory levels, and break-fix for our robotics kiosks.

Hillman's corporate headquarters is located at 1280 Kemper Meadow Drive, Cincinnati, Ohio. We maintain a website at www.hillmangroup.com. Information contained or linked on our website is not incorporated by reference into this annual report and should not be considered a part of this annual report.

In 1964, Max Hillman established Hillman Bolt & Screw Corporation in Cincinnati, Ohio when he purchased a franchise operation from Sharon Bolt & Screw, a hardware fastener company. Max began distributing fasteners to independent hardware stores in southern Ohio and northern Kentucky, with a relentless commitment to service.

Max's two sons, Mick Hillman and Rick Hillman, joined their father's company in 1969, as Hillman's customer base and distribution network continued to grow. In 1982, Hillman Bolt & Screw was purchased by Sun Distributors followed by Max's retirement shortly thereafter. Mick and Rick took over the day-to-day operations of the business in 1984.

During the early 1990s, the Company developed its National Field Service Group, which today includes over 1,200 field service and sales representatives, to manage the complex assortment of Hillman products on its customers' shelves. Over the next three decades Hillman continued to win new business, expanding from traditional hardware stores to big box and home improvement retailers, and into adjacent product categories through multiple strategic acquisitions.

During the 2000s, Hillman was purchased three separate times by private equity firms (2001, 2004 and 2010). During 2012 and 2013, Rick and Mick Hillman retired, respectively, after more than 40 years of actively managing the Company. Thereafter in 2014, CCMP Capital Advisors acquired the majority interest in Hillman. In 2021, Hillman became a publicly traded company, listing its shares on the Nasdaq stock exchange under the ticker symbol "HLMN" by virtue of a merger with a Special Purpose Acquisition Company ("SPAC").
Hillman's legacy of service has remained unchanged throughout its history, and it continues to take care of its customers first.
We are comprised of three separate operating business segments: (1) Hardware and Protective Solutions, (2) Robotics and Digital Solutions, and (3) Canada.

We provide products such as fasteners and related hardware items; threaded rod and metal shapes; keys and key duplication systems; builder's hardware; rope and chain; protective solutions, such as gloves, eye-wear, and cleaning rags; and identification items, such as tags and letters, numbers, and signs to retail outlets, primarily hardware stores, home centers and mass merchants, pet supply stores, grocery stores, and drug stores. We complement our extensive product selection with regular retailer visits by our field sales and service organization.

We market and distribute a wide variety of Stock Keeping Units ("SKUs") of small, hard-to-find and hard-to-manage hardware items. We function as a category manager for retailers and support these products with in-store service, high order fill rates, and rapid delivery of products sold. Sales and service representatives regularly visit retail outlets to review stock levels, reorder items in need of replacement, and interact with the store management to offer new product and merchandising ideas. Thousands of items can be actively managed with the retailer experiencing a substantial reduction of in-store labor costs and replenishment paperwork. Service representatives also assist in organizing the products in a consumer-friendly manner. We complement our broad range of products with merchandising services such as displays, product identification stickers, retail price labels, store rack and drawer systems, assistance in rack positioning and store layout, and inventory restocking services. We regularly refresh retailers' displays with new products and package designs utilizing color-coding to simplify the shopping experience for consumers and improve the attractiveness of individual store displays.

We operate from 24 strategically located distribution centers in North America and supplement our operations with third-party logistics providers to warehouse and ship customer orders in the certain areas.

Our product strategy concentrates on providing total project solutions using the latest technology for common and unique home improvement projects. Our portfolio provides retailers the assurance that their shoppers can find the right product at the right price within an 'easy to shop' environment.

We currently manage a worldwide supply chain comprised of a large number of vendors, the largest of which accounted for approximately 7.6% of the Company's annual purchases and the top five of which accounted for approximately 17.2% of our annual purchases. Our vendor quality control procedures include on-site evaluations and frequent product testing. Vendors are also evaluated based on delivery performance and the accuracy of their shipments.

Our Hardware and Protective Solutions segment includes a variety of product categories including: Fasteners; Builders Hardware; Wall Hanging, Threaded Rod and Metal Shapes; Rope and Chain; Letters, Numbers, and Signs ("LNS"); and Personal Protective Equipment, such as gloves and eye-wear.

headings: Risks Relating to Our Products and Demand for our Products:

Our sales are dependent upon the health and stability of the general economy. Adverse changes in economic factors specific to the home improvement industry may adversely affect our sales and financial performance.
Large customer concentration and the inability to penetrate new channels of distribution could adversely affect our business.
To compete successfully, we must develop and commercialize a continuing stream of innovative new products that create consumer demand.
Our business is subject to risks associated with sourcing product from overseas, including tariffs.
Our results of operations could be negatively impacted by inflation or deflation in supply chain costs, including raw materials, sourcing, transportation and energy.
We are subject to inventory management risks: insufficient inventory may result in increased costs, lost sales and lost customers, while excess inventory may increase our costs.
Because our business is working capital intensive, we rely on our ability to manage our product purchasing and customer credit policies.
We are subject to the risks of doing business internationally.
Successful sales and marketing efforts depend on our ability to recruit and retain qualified employees.
Increases in labor costs, potential labor disputes and work stoppages or an inability to hire skilled distribution, sales and other personnel could adversely affect our business.
Risks Related to our Technology and Cybersecurity:
Our success is highly dependent on information and our technology systems, as well as those of our third party vendors and business partners.
Complications with the design or implementation of our new enterprise resource planning ("ERP") system could adversely impact our business and operations.
Failure to adequately protect intellectual property could adversely affect our business.
Our success depends in part on our ability to operate without infringing on or misappropriating the proprietary rights of others, and if we are unable to do so we may be liable for damages.
We have significant indebtedness that could affect operations and financial condition and prevent us from successfully executing our strategy.
Despite current indebtedness levels, we may still be able to incur substantially more debt. This could further exacerbate the risks associated with our substantial leverage.
We are subject to fluctuations in interest rates.
The failure to meet certain financial covenants required by our credit agreements may materially and adversely affect assets, financial position, and cash flows.
Volatility and weakness in bank and capital markets may adversely affect credit availability and related financing costs for us.
Legal, Regulatory, and Other External Risks:
We are exposed to adverse changes in currency exchange rates.
If we were required to write down all or part of our goodwill or indefinite-lived trade names, our financial condition and results of operations could be materially adversely affected.
We are subject to legal proceedings and legal compliance risks.
Our business may be adversely affected by seasonality.
Future tax law changes may materially increase our prospective income tax expense.
paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risks. However, the risks set forth below are not the only risks that we face, and we face other risks which have not yet been identified or which are not yet otherwise predictable. If any of the following risks occur or are otherwise realized, our business, financial condition, and results of operations could be materially adversely affected. You should carefully consider the risks described below and all other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our Consolidated Financial Statements and the related Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements and schedules thereto.

Many North American and global economic factors may adversely affect our financial performance. These include, but are not limited to, periods of slow economic growth or recession, home price appreciation or decreasing housing turnover, volatility and/or lack of liquidity from time to time in U.S. and world financial markets and the consequent reduced availability and/or higher cost of borrowing to Hillman, its customers, and consumers, slower rates of growth in real disposable personal income that could affect the rate of growth in consumer spending, inflation and its impacts on discretionary spending and on our costs, shortages, and other disruptions in the labor supply, consumer debt levels, changes in tax rates and policy, outbreak of pandemics, fluctuations in fuel and energy costs, inflation or deflation of commodity prices, natural disasters, armed conflicts, and acts of both domestic and international terrorism.

Sales of many of our products are driven by the activity level of home repair and remodel projects. Our customers, suppliers, and other parties with whom we do business are also impacted by the foregoing conditions and adverse changes may result in financial difficulties leading to restructurings, bankruptcies, liquidations, and other unfavorable events for our customers, consumers, suppliers, and other service providers. Adverse trends in any of the foregoing factors could reduce our sales, adversely impact the mix of our sales, or increase our costs, which could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Our two largest customers constituted approximately $674.3 million of net sales and $33.0 million of the year-end accounts receivable balance for 2025. Both of these customers are big box chain stores. Our results of operations depend greatly on our ability to maintain existing relationships and arrangements with these big box chain stores. To the extent that the big box chain stores are materially adversely impacted by the changing retail landscape, this could have a negative effect on our results of operations. These two customers have been key components of our growth and failure to maintain fulfillment and service levels or relationships with these customers could result in a material loss of business. Our inability to penetrate new channels of distribution, including ecommerce, may also have a negative impact on our future sales and business (see Note 17 - Concentration of Credit Risks of the Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for additional information).

If a large customer experiences a material decline in its business, that could have a negative impact on our ability to collect outstanding accounts receivable or continue future sales and business with that customer, which could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition, results of operations, and ability to generate future sales and cash flow from that customer. This occurred on October 14, 2024, when True Value Company, LLC and certain of its affiliates (collectively, "True Value"), filed a voluntary petition for relief under Chapter 11 of the United States Bankruptcy Code that impaired the collectability of our accounts receivable and resulted in us recording a charge of $8.6 million in 2024.

Our long-term success in the current competitive environment depends on our ability to develop and commercialize a continuing stream of innovative new products which create and maintain consumer demand. We also face the risk that our competitors will introduce innovative new products that compete with our products. Our strategy includes increased investment in new product development and continued focus on innovation. There are, nevertheless, numerous uncertainties inherent in successfully developing and commercializing innovative new products on a continuing basis, and new product launches may not provide expected growth results.

paragraphs: Net sales during 2025 increased by 5.4% when compared to 2024. Driving our performance for the year was the net sales contributions from new business wins, along with the contribution of net sales from the Intex DIY acquisition, which closed in August 2024, and the contribution of price increases, which were implemented during the year to offset an increase in costs related to tariffs. These contributions to net sales were offset by the soft home improvement market during the year. Hardware and Protective Solutions, our largest segment making up 76.9% of our net sales, led the way with an increase of 7.8%, while our Robotics and Digital Solutions segment returned to growth during 2025 contributing 1.6%. Partially offsetting this growth was a decline in our Canadian business segment.

Products across our business are primarily used by DIYers and professionals shopping at our customers' retail locations for repair, maintenance, and remodel projects. Because repair and maintenance projects are beneficial and often necessary no matter the economic environment, we believe our business is generally resilient to economic downturns. However, remodel projects are more dependent upon macroeconomic variables, including existing home sales. According to the National Association of Realtors, existing home sales in the U.S. for 2025 were unchanged from 2024, which marked a 30-year low, totaling 4.1 million. This was a headwind for our top line results during the year.

Our competitive moat, which consists of our 1,200 member field sales and service team, our ability to ship direct to the retail locations of our customers rather than their distribution network, and our 60+ years of experience set us apart from the competition. As such, we launched multiple new business wins during the year and we won vendor of the year awards from Do It Best and Home Depot Canada. We continue to focus on taking great care of our customers which has been a key focus on the company for over 60-years.

We are pleased with our top and bottom line results during 2025, as both were records for Hillman. Producing record top and bottom line results while successfully managing the dynamic and complex tariff situation is a testament to our team. Looking to 2026, we remain committed to driving value for our stakeholders, taking great care of our customers, and continuing to grow our business.

paragraphs: Hillman Solutions Corp. 以及其百分之百持股之子公司（合稱為 "Hillman" 或 "本公司"）為北美零售市場中最大之硬體相關產品及相關商品服務供應商之一。本公司之主要業務由本公司百分之百持股之子公司 Hillman 進行，該子公司於 2025 年之淨銷售額約為 1,552.2 百萬美元。Hillman 將其產品銷售至美國、加拿大、墨西哥、拉丁美洲及加勒比地區之五金店、家居中心、大型零售商、寵物用品店及其他零售通路。產品線包括數千種小零組件，如螺絲釘及相關硬體用品；螺紋桿及金屬型材；鑰匙；建築用五金；個人防護裝備，如手套及眼鏡；繩索及鏈條；以及識別用品，如標籤及字母、數字與標誌。我們透過設計與安裝商品展示系統、維持適當之零售店存貨水準及提供機器人自動販賣機之維修服務來支援產品銷售。
本公司之總部位於俄亥俄州辛辛那提市 1280 Kemper Meadow Drive。本公司維護網站於 www.hillmangroup.com。網站上所載或連結之資訊未經引用為本年度報告之組成部分，亦不應視為本年度報告之一部分。
1964 年，Max Hillman 在俄亥俄州辛辛那提市創立 Hillman Bolt & Screw Corporation，當時他從 Sharon Bolt & Screw 公司購入特許經營權，該公司為一家硬體緊固件公司。Max 開始將緊固件分銷至俄亥俄州南部及肯塔基州北部之獨立五金店，並以對服務的無比承諾為其經營特色。
Max 之兩位兒子 Mick Hillman 與 Rick Hillman 於 1969 年加入其父親之公司，當時 Hillman 之客戶羣與分銷網路持續擴張。1982 年，Hillman Bolt & Screw 被 Sun Distributors 收購，隨後 Max 便退休。Mick 與 Rick 於 1984 年接掌公司之日常營運。
在 1990 年代初期，本公司發展出其國家現場服務羣組，該羣組今日包含逾 1,200 名現場服務與銷售代表，用以管理客戶貨架上複雜的 Hillman 產品組合。接下來的三十年中，Hillman 繼續獲取新業務，從傳統五金店擴展至大型零售與家居改善零售商，並透過多項戰略收購進入相關產品類別。

在 2000 年代，Hillman 三次被私人股權公司收購（2001 年、2004 年與 2010 年）。2012 年與 2013 年，Rick 與 Mick Hillman 依序退休，他們在本公司積極經營逾 40 年。隨後於 2014 年，CCMP Capital Advisors 收購 Hillman 之大多數股權。2021 年，Hillman 成為上市公司，其股票於納斯達克股票交易所上市交易，股票代碼為 "HLMN"，此為與特殊目的收購公司（"SPAC"）合併所致。
Hillman 服務之傳統延續至今未變，並持續以顧客為先。
本公司由三個獨立運作之業務分部組成：（1）硬體與防護解決方案、（2）機械人與數位解決方案、（3）加拿大。
本公司提供產品如螺絲與相關五金配件；螺紋桿與金屬型材；鑰匙與鑰匙複製系統；建築用五金；繩索與鏈條；防護解決方案，如手套、眼鏡與清潔布；以及識別用品，如標籤與字母、數字與標誌，銷售至零售通路，主要包括五金店、居家中心與大型零售商、寵物用品店、超級市場與藥妝店。本公司以廣泛的產品選擇搭配現場銷售與服務團隊定期造訪零售商。

本公司行銷與分銷大量庫存單位（"SKUs"）的小型、難尋且難以管理的五金產品。本公司為零售商擔任類別管理，並透過店內服務、高訂單履行率與快速配送支援這些產品。銷售與服務代表定期造訪零售通路，審視庫存量、更換需補貨的商品，並與店長互動，提供新產品與商品陳列建議。零售商可有效管理數千項商品，並大幅降低店內人力成本與補貨文件工作。服務代表亦協助以消費者友善方式整理商品。本公司以廣泛的商品種類搭配商品陳列服務，如展示架、商品標籤、零售價格標籤、店內架與抽屜系統、協助架位與店內佈局，以及庫存補貨服務。本公司定期為零售商更新展示架，使用新產品與包裝設計，並透過色彩編碼簡化消費者購物經驗，並提升單店展示的吸引力。
本公司在北美地區擁有24個戰略位置的配送中心，並透過第三方物流業者補充運營，用以倉儲與發送客戶訂單。
本公司產品策略著重於透過最新技術，為常見與獨特的居家改善工程提供完整的解決方案。本公司產品組合讓零售商確信其消費者可在"易於購物"的環境中，以正確價格找到正確產品。
本公司目前管理一個全球供應鏈，包含大量供應商，其中最大的供應商佔本公司年度採購約7.6%，前五大供應商則佔年度採購約17.2%。本公司供應商品質控制程序包括現場評估與頻繁產品測試。供應商亦根據其交貨表現與貨運準確性進行評估。
本公司五金與防護解決方案應報告分部包含多種產品類別，包括：零組件；建築用五金；牆面掛設、螺紋桿與金屬型材；繩索與鏈條；字母、數字與標誌（"LNS"）；以及個人防護裝備，如手套與眼鏡。

paragraphs: 淨銷售額於 2025 年較 2024 年成長 5.4%。驅動我們全年表現的是來自新業務獲勝的淨銷售額貢獻，以及來自 Intex DIY 收購案的淨銷售額貢獻，該收購案於 2024 年 8 月完成，還有來自價格調漲的淨銷售額貢獻，這些調漲於本年實施以抵銷與關稅相關成本的增加。這些淨銷售額貢獻被本年軟弱的住宅改善市場所抵銷。我們最大的應報告分部為 Hardware and Protective Solutions，佔我們淨銷售額的 76.9%，帶領成長 7.8%，而我們的 Robotics and Digital Solutions 分部於 2025 年恢復成長，貢獻 1.6%。部分抵銷此成長的是加拿大業務分部的下滑。
本公司各項產品主要用於 DIY 者及專業人士在客戶零售門市購買，用於修繕、維護及整修工程。由於修繕與維護工程無論經濟環境如何皆屬有益且常為必要，我們認為本公司業務通常能抵禦經濟衰退。然而，整修工程較依賴總體經濟變數，包括現有住宅銷售數量。根據美國房地產協會資料，美國 2025 年現有住宅銷售量與 2024 年相同，為 30 年來最低，總計 4.1 百萬。此為本公司年度營收表現的負面因素。
我們的競爭優勢包含我們 1,200 名成員的現場銷售與服務團隊、我們能直接將產品運送到客戶零售據點而非其配送網路的能力，以及我們 60 多年的經驗。因此，我們於本年推出了多項新業務獲勝，並獲得了 Do It Best 和 Home Depot Canada 的年度最佳供應商獎項。我們持續著重於照顧客戶，這已成為公司超過 60 年來的重點。
我們對 2025 年的營收與淨利表現感到滿意，因為這兩者皆為 Hillman 的紀錄。在成功管理動態且複雜的關稅情況下，同時創造出營收與淨利的紀錄，這證明瞭我們團隊的實力。展望 2026 年，我們仍致力於為股東創造價值、照顧客戶，並持續成長業務。

headings: 與我們產品及產品需求相關的風險：
我們的銷售取決於總體經濟的健康與穩定。住宅改善產業特定的經濟因素惡化可能不利於我們的銷售與財務表現。
大型客戶集中度及無法滲透新的分銷渠道可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
為成功競爭，我們必須持續開發並商業化創新產品，以創造消費者需求。
與我們營運相關的風險：
我們的業務面臨來自海外採購產品的風險，包括關稅。
本公司營運成果可能因供應鏈成本的通貨膨脹或通貨緊縮而受到負面影響，包括原材料、採購、運輸及能源等成本。
本公司面臨存貨管理風險：存貨不足可能導致成本增加、銷售減少及客戶流失，而存貨過多則可能增加本公司成本。
由於本公司業務屬營運資金密集型，因此依賴本公司管理產品採購及客戶信用政策的能力。
本公司面臨國際業務的風險。
與本公司員工相關的風險：
銷售與市場推廣成效的達成，依賴本公司招募及留住合資格員工的能力。
勞動成本增加、潛在的勞動糾紛及罷工或無法聘僱具備技能的配送、銷售及其他人員，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
與本公司科技及網路安全相關的風險：
本公司之成功高度依賴資訊及本公司科技系統，以及第三方供應商及商業夥伴之系統。
本公司新企業資源規劃（"ERP"）系統之設計或實施出現問題，可能對本公司業務及營運造成不利影響。
與智慧財產權相關的風險：
未能充分保護智慧財產權，可能對本公司業務造成不利影響。
本公司之成功在部分程度上取決於能否在營運中不侵犯或不不當使用他人的專有權利，若無法做到此點，本公司可能需對損害賠償負責任。
與本公司負債相關之風險：
本公司負有重大負債，此負債可能影響營運及財務狀況，並可能阻礙本公司成功執行其策略。
儘管目前負債水準已相當高，本公司仍可能進一步負擔大量負債。此舉可能進一步加劇與本公司重大負債相關之風險。
本公司受利率波動之影響。
未能符合信用協議所要求之某些財務約束條款，可能對資產、財務狀況及現金流造成重大且不利之影響。
銀行及資本市場之波動與疲軟可能對本公司之信貸取得及相關融資成本造成不利影響。
法律、法規及其他外部風險：
我們面臨匯率變動不利的風險。
若我們需對全部或部分 goodwill 或無限期壽命的商標進行減值提列，將可能對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
我們面臨法律訴訟及法律合規風險。
我們的業務可能因季節性因素而受到不利影響。
未來稅法變更可能導致我們未來所得稅費用大幅增加。
paragraphs: 您應謹慎考慮下列風險。然而，下列所列風險並非我們所面臨的唯一風險，我們還可能面臨其他尚未識別或尚未預測的風險。如果任何上述風險發生或實現，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。您應謹慎考慮下列所列風險，以及本年度報告表10-K中所有其他資訊，包括我們的合併財務報表及相關合併財務報表附註與附表。

許多北美及全球經濟因素可能對我們的財務表現造成不利影響。這些因素包括，但不僅限於，經濟成長緩慢或衰退期、住宅價格上漲或住宅交易量減少、美國及全球財務市場的波動性及/或流動性不足，以及對Hillman及其客戶與消費者而言，貸款取得的減少及/或成本提高、實質個人可支配收入成長率減緩可能影響消費者支出成長率、通貨膨脹及其對可支配支出及我們成本的影響、勞動力供應短缺及其他幹擾、消費者負債水平、稅率與政策的變動、疫情爆發、燃料與能源成本的波動、商品價格的通貨膨脹或通貨緊縮、天然災害、軍事衝突，以及國內外恐怖攻擊行為。
我們許多產品的銷售取決於住宅修繕與翻新工程的活動程度。我們的客戶、供應商及其他與我們有業務往來的機構也受到上述條件的影響，不利的變化可能導致財務困難，進而引發重整、破產、清算及其他對我們客戶、消費者、供應商及其他服務提供者的不利事件。上述任何因素的不利趨勢可能減少我們的銷售、對我們銷售組成造成不利影響，或提高我們的成本，這可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。

若主要客戶之業務出現重大衰退，可能對本公司收取應收帳款或持續與該客戶進行未來銷售與業務之能力產生負面影響，進而對本公司財務狀況、營運成果及從該客戶產生未來銷售與現金流之能力造成重大不利影響。此情形於2024年10月14日發生，當時True Value Company, LLC及其部分附屬公司（合稱「True Value」）根據美國破產法第11章提出自願重整申請，導致本公司應收帳款之可收回性受損，並使本公司於2024年計提8.6 百萬美元之費用。
我們在現有競爭環境中長遠的成功取決於我們開發並商業化持續創新產品的能力，這些產品能創造並維持消費者需求。我們也面臨競爭對手推出創新產品與我們產品競爭的風險。我們的策略包括增加新產品開發的投資，並持續專注於創新。然而，成功持續開發與商業化創新產品仍存在許多不確定性，新產品發佈可能不會達到預期的成長成果。
